> **Deprecated — see below for the updated review.**

<details><summary>Previous review (2026-09-17)</summary>

**Automated review note — AI-generated (Claude), validated against the live diff.** Please sanity-check before acting.

Reviewed at head `01aa011dbe` — first AI review of this PR.

Full report, with everything that was checked: https://uav.tridgell.net/DevCallReviews/2026_09_18_AIReview/devcall_pr_reviews.html#prAPReview-2

**Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES** — the mechanism is sound; what is missing is the other half of the rename.

The switch itself is in good shape and unusually well tested. It uses the correct `ln -sfn` + `mv -T` idiom under `flock`, with verification and revert — which is the single most likely concrete bug in a change described this way, and it is right at every call site. Both reviewers ran the suite (**193 passed, 37 subtests**) and the PR's own mutation harness (**80 of 80 mutations caught, 0 unaccounted for**), including `noflock`, `earlyrelease`, `lazyswitch`, `noswitchback` and `lyingrevert`. `~/review/auth/` already carries the documented link layout, so there is no un-migrated-box problem for the `default` or `rsync` roles on merge.

The problem is that `runner/bin/make-runs-page.py` is not in this PR's 8 changed files, and it is still built around the variables and statuses this PR replaces. Since merging this repo *is* the deploy, that lands the same minute.

### Blockers

- `runner/bin/make-runs-page.py:220` — **the dashboard finds Claude transcripts through `REVIEW_RSYNC_CLAUDE_DIR`, which this PR deletes, so the selected account's usage stops being counted.** `_roots = ['~/.claude', os.environ.get('REVIEW_RSYNC_CLAUDE_DIR', '~/review/etc/claude-rsync')]`, and the `export` is gone from `review-env.sh`, so the lookup falls through to a directory that does not exist on this box. The account that role uses today is `~/review/auth/claude-personal`, with 28 `*.jsonl` transcripts, none of which are counted — demonstrated by placing a synthetic 123-input-token transcript under `auth/claude-personal` (ignored) and then under `~/.claude` (counted). Run this PR's headline command `review-auth.sh use claude default personal` and the whole main workload moves somewhere the dashboard has never heard of, exactly when someone is watching it because a quota ran out. Fix: derive `_roots` from the auth layout — `~/.claude` plus every `$REVIEW_AUTH/claude-*/` directory, skipping the role links, as `review-auth.sh list` already does.

- `runner/bin/make-runs-page.py:77` — **this PR introduces `status=wrong-codex-account` but the dashboard recognises only the Claude equivalent, so a refused run displays as still running for ever.** The status is echoed at six sites in `run-reviewprs.sh` and asserted in `runner/tests/test_runner_guard.py`, while `make-runs-page.py:77` matches only `status=wrong-claude-account`. Feeding the actual dashboard a completed log with the new status leaves the row marked `running` with an ever-increasing elapsed time, excluded from the failure totals. The guard exists precisely so a run refuses rather than spending the wrong subscription — a refusal that reads as a hung job is the wrong way round.

- `runner/bin/make-runs-page.py:113` — **the Codex weekly-quota meter reads only `~/.codex/sessions`, so switching the Codex account loses quota visibility the same way.** The glob is hardcoded, with no awareness of `CODEX_HOME` or of the role-selected account directories this PR introduces: a synthetic 42% weekly sample under another account produced no reading, and the identical file exposed through `~/.codex` produced 42%. Same defect as the Claude one above; account discovery and quota attribution want fixing together.

### Issues

- `README.md:106` — the README still documents what this PR removes. The `local.conf` variable table has a `REVIEW_RSYNC_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` row, and "The second target" still tells you to set it in `local.conf` and sign in with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/review/etc/claude-rsync claude auth login` (`:137`, `:141`), while `runner/etc/local.conf.example` now says "Accounts are not configured here". Following the README on a fresh box gives no `auth/claude-rsync`, and because a non-default role deliberately never falls back, the first `run-reviewprs.sh rsync` exits `FATAL: cannot use the claude account for role rsync` — reproduced in an isolated home with exactly the documented legacy setup — so the 05:25 cron entry silently stops producing reviews. This is live, not hypothetical: `~/review/etc/local.conf` on this box still assigns the obsolete variable, now inert. Same class, smaller: `docs/review-box.md:18` still lists `~/review/etc/` as holding "per-account config" and has no `~/review/auth/` row in its path table, and `:51` still describes configuring an account in `local.conf`.

- `runner/bin/claude-usage-probe.sh:19` — the hourly probe never resolves a role, so after a switch it keeps sampling the wrong account. It sources `review-env.sh` but calls `claude auth status` and `claude -p /usage` with whatever cron gives it, so it always reads `~/.claude`. That was defensible when only `rsync` mode could differ and `run-reviewprs.sh` exported `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` around its own probes; after `review-auth.sh use claude default personal` the hourly trace records the old account's meter while every run burns the new one, and since the probe tags each reading with the account it read, one meter is frozen and the other is never sampled between runs. Reproduced with an isolated home and a stub CLI. One caution: a fix must preserve the runner's explicitly selected environment for its own before/after probes — unconditionally selecting `default` would misdirect the rsync probes.

- `runner/bin/review-env.sh:342-353` — the whole `# --- publishing ---` block is present twice, byte-identical, with the "Site configuration..." comment stranded between the copies at 340-341. New in this PR: `origin/main` has one `^# --- publishing` marker, this head has two. Harmless — all four assignments are idempotent `${X:-}` exports and the second copy does *not* re-run `hostname` (instrumenting it showed exactly one invocation across both blocks) — but it is a copy-paste artefact in the file every review-box process sources. Deleting 340-353 fixes it.

_Two notes are in the report rather than here: `check_codex_config` will refuse a run over a `[model_providers.*]` table that nothing selects (reproduced), though it does **not** refuse on this box — `check_codex_config ~/.codex` at this head produces no diagnostic and `review-auth.sh status` reports healthy roles, so there is no config-related deployment blocker; and the confirmatory test/mutation run above._

---
Reviewed by: Claude (full read of the diff, thread and surrounding source, plus running the suite and the mutation harness) + an independent `codex exec` pass given only this PR's number and findings. Codex: 3 confirmed, 3 adjusted, 0 refuted, **2 new blockers added** — the `:77` and `:113` items above are its findings, confirmed here against the head file and the PR diff.


</details>

> **Deprecated — see below for the updated review.**

<details><summary>Previous review (2026-09-18)</summary>

**Automated review note — AI-generated (Claude), validated against the live diff.** Please sanity-check before acting.

Full report: [https://uav.tridgell.net/DevCallReviews/2026_09_18/devcall_pr_reviews.html#prAPReview-2](https://uav.tridgell.net/DevCallReviews/2026_09_18/devcall_pr_reviews.html#prAPReview-2)

Re-reviewed at head `3a5588b3f7`. **Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES** — on one new finding, not on anything from last round.

### Previous round: all five closed

Commit `3a5588b3` answers every finding from `01aa011dbe`, and I re-verified each at this head rather than taking the commit message for it:

| Previous finding | Status |
|---|---|
| **Blocker** dashboard found transcripts via the deleted `REVIEW_RSYNC_CLAUDE_DIR` | **RESOLVED** — `account_dirs()` enumerates `~/.<tool>` plus every real `$REVIEW_AUTH/<tool>-*` directory; three mutations pin it |
| **Blocker** `status=wrong-codex-account` unrecognised, refusal shown as "running" for ever | **RESOLVED** — matched by shape now, with a test asserting both that `wrong-account` appears and that `>running<` does not |
| **Blocker** Codex weekly meter hardcoded to `~/.codex/sessions` | **RESOLVED** for discovery; one residual hole, finding 3 below |
| **Issue** README and `docs/review-box.md` still documented `REVIEW_RSYNC_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT` | **RESOLVED** — repo-wide grep finds no remaining reference. Two stale *comments* remain, finding 6 |
| **Issue** hourly probe never resolved a role | **RESOLVED**, and the stated caveat respected — it resolves only when both `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `REVIEW_ROLE` are unset, so a run's own probes stay on the account the run selected. Both branches tested |
| Note: duplicated `publishing` block | **RESOLVED** — four section markers, one `publishing` |

The test story is genuinely strong and both reviewers checked it independently: **206 tests pass** (up from 193) and **`mutate.py` catches 86 of 86 mutations** (up from 80), with each mutation tied to a named regression test that must produce a `FAIL` rather than an `ERROR` — real mutation testing, not assertion-by-construction. CI wiring read rather than assumed: `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs `bash -n` over the shell scripts, `compileall`, and every `runner/tests/test_*.py`, so all three new test files do run. (`mutate.py` does not, being ~9 minutes and not named `test_*` — reasonable, but it means a mutation regression is only caught by hand.)

### What blocks

**BUG — `run-reviewprs.sh:77` and `:91` — a refused run writes no log at all.** The two account pre-flight FATALs this PR adds exit *before* `exec >>"$LOG" 2>&1` at `:132`, and before `LOG` is even assigned at `:112`. With `MAILTO=""` in `runner/etc/crontab.reviewprs:8` the diagnostic is discarded, and since the dashboard builds its rows from `$REVIEW_LOGS/reviewprs-*.log` there is no row either — not even `wrong-account`.

This is a **regression from the base branch**, and since that is the load-bearing claim I checked it directly rather than taking it from either agent: on `origin/main` the two `status=wrong-claude-account` exits are at lines 177 and 185, well after the redirect at line 99. At this head two new ones sit at 77 and 91, before the redirect at 132; every other such exit (248 onwards) is still after it. Both reviewers separately reproduced the silent exit in an isolated `$HOME` with a dangling `auth/claude-rsync` link.

It also undercuts this PR's own promise at `README.md:150` that "a missing `rsync` link is an error rather than a silent fall back" — it *is* an error, but an invisible one, which in practice is the 05:25 rsync slot going quiet with nothing to look at.

The suite cannot catch it: all 78 guard tests invoke the extracted guard with `--dry-run`, and `--dry-run` skips the redirect (`:130`).

**Fix:** move the `clear_inherited_credentials` / `select_account` block to just after the banner and before the EXIT trap — that still chooses the account before anything spends quota and before the trap takes its closing reading — and add one non-`--dry-run` test asserting the refusal lands in `$REVIEW_LOGS`.

### Other findings

**ISSUE — `make-runs-page.py:242-248` — transcripts counted twice when `~/.claude` is a symlink into an account directory.** `_files` and `_codex_sessions` dedupe by glob *path string*, not by realpath, and `account_dirs()` adds `~/.<tool>` unconditionally while filtering only symlinks found under `auth/`. Both reviewers reproduced it: one 5–6M-token transcript renders as double. That layout is not hypothetical — `review-env.sh:215` (`[ ! -L "$own" ]`) and `review-auth.sh` both go out of their way to support it. *Scope, which neither agent stated:* the live box today is the other way round (`auth/claude-ardupilot -> ~/.claude`, a symlink, correctly skipped), so this is latent rather than currently mis-reporting — it starts biting the moment someone points `~/.claude` into `auth/`, which is the migration this PR is for. Fix: `realpath` before the set union, or dedupe `account_dirs()` by realpath.

**ISSUE — `make-runs-page.py:133-136` — quota readings from different Codex subscriptions merge into one unlabelled meter.** `_codex_sessions` is a flat comprehension over `account_dirs('codex')` and nothing downstream carries the account, so a fixture with account A at 10 % and account B at 90 % attributed an 80-point rise to a run on A. Latent today (one real Codex directory), but multiple accounts is exactly what this PR exists to enable, and a wrong quota meter is what drives the decision to switch. Found by the cold pass only.

**ISSUE — `run-reviewprs.sh:83` — the validated directory is discarded and the role resolved a second time.** `select_account` calls `review_auth`, checks its return code… then throws `d` away and calls `role_config_dir`, which re-resolves and, on any error, falls back to `readlink -f "$HOME/.$tool"` (`review-env.sh:211-218`). A switch landing between the two reads yields the default account with the rc check already passed. The two reviewers disagreed here and I read both halves myself: your *switching-under-a-live-run* design is genuinely safe — the resolved real path is what gets exported, so repointing the link mid-run cannot move a running tool, and that clearance stands. The race is only in the narrower gap before the export, it is microseconds wide, and the cold agent could reproduce it only by repointing deterministically between the reads — hence ISSUE, not BUG. One-line fix: reuse the `d` `review_auth` already returned.

**NOTE — `review-auth.sh:246` and `:314`** — tool, role and account names are interpolated into paths without validation: `use claude 'foo/../../work/victim' personal` succeeds and creates a role symlink and lock under `review/work`, and `login` with a `..`-bearing account name creates a directory outside `auth/`. Operator-typed footguns rather than a vulnerability — roles are not user input (`ROLES="default rsync"`) and the containment check refuses the result later — but a `case "$name" in *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) refuse` guard plus `umask 077` before the `mkdir` closes both cheaply. *(The cold pass called this a BUG; I have kept it a NOTE for the reason above.)*

**NOTE — `run-reviewprs.sh:451`** — the runner launches the reviewing agent with `--add-dir "$REVIEW_ROOT"` and `--permission-mode auto`, and this PR makes `$REVIEW_ROOT/auth/` the documented home of every account's credentials, so `auth/claude-personal/.credentials.json` is now inside the agent's granted directory — same uid, mode 600 notwithstanding — while that agent reads untrusted pull-request content. Partly pre-existing, but the old *default* account lived in `~/.claude`, outside the root, and this PR moves it in. Given the PR's framing is credential isolation, worth settling now: a `Read`/`Bash` deny for `~/review/auth/**` in the pre-flight's required rule list, or `auth/` outside `$REVIEW_ROOT`.

**NOTE — `runner/tests/test_runs_page.py:95`** — the refusal and running fixtures hardcode 2026-09-18 while the dashboard filters against the real current date (`make-runs-page.py:20-21`, discarded at `:66`). These tests will start failing on their own once that window passes. Generate the timestamps relative to `now`, or freeze the clock.

**NOTE — `review-env.sh:297-299` and `:356-358`** — two comment blocks still describe the design this PR replaces: a `# --- per-mode Claude account ---` header now sitting above `clear_stale_oauth_lock` with nothing per-mode under it, and a site-configuration header still saying `local.conf` holds "the Claude account a given mode runs as", which `local.conf.example:21` now explicitly denies.

**NOTE — `run-reviewprs.sh:77`** — `select_account` emits `status=wrong-claude-account` for both tools, so a broken *codex* role logs a claude status. Display is unaffected now that the dashboard matches by shape; `status=wrong-$tool-account` is a one-line fix.

### Checked and cleared

**The environment contract survives** — `REVIEW_DATA`, `REVIEW_REPOS`, `REVIEW_PUBLISH`, `RSYNC_AUTH`, `REVIEW_PUBLIC_URL`, `REVIEW_BOX_NAME`, `TMPDIR`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `CCACHE_DIR`, `NODE_PATH` all still exported with the same names and meanings, `REVIEW_AUTH` added. Nothing that would silently skip publishing or land scratch on tmpfs. **`REVIEW_COMMENT_ACCOUNTS` is untouched** — a gap there would make every pre-switch review comment invisible and double-comment every tracked PR, so it was checked end to end.

**The switch itself**: `ln -sfn --` into a temp name then `mv -T` under a per-role `flock`, with post-switch re-resolution, revert, and an honest "COULD NOT REVERT" when the revert fails; the root check and `[ ! -L "$lockf" ]` run before the lock file is opened, so a truncating open cannot be aimed through a symlink. Nine named mutations pin those guards.

**No secret reaches a log, a command line or a publish path**: `clear_inherited_credentials` prints variable *names* only; `read_account_file` rejects anything that is not a short address or uuid, so an `ACCOUNT` symlinked at a credentials file cannot echo a token; `check_codex_config` prints setting keys, `ascii()`-escaped and capped; `login` only prints the command for the operator to run; publishing is from `$REVIEW_ROOT/work`. Both reviewers checked this separately and agreed.

**Crontab**: the only change is `REVIEWPRS_LOCK_WAIT` 1800 → 7200 on the followup line, with a documented reason; all five entries still invoke the same script paths and modes, and `rsync` still maps to `ROLE=rsync`, now also case-insensitively and for the full PR-URL form. **Guard semantics**: the `claude auth status --json` chain requires all three of `authMethod`/`apiProvider`/`configDirectory`, refuses anything but `claude.ai` + `firstParty`, refuses a config directory other than the selected one, refuses a CLI that exited non-zero even if it emitted JSON, and refuses when an `ACCOUNT` record exists but the identity cannot be determined — with seven mutations pinning it, and `review-auth.sh status` making the same judgements.


</details>

> **Deprecated — see below for the updated review.**

<details><summary>Previous review (2026-09-18)</summary>

**Automated review note — AI-generated (Claude), validated against the live diff.** Please sanity-check before acting.

Full report, with what was checked and found clean: https://uav.tridgell.net/DevCallReviews/2026_09_18/devcall_pr_reviews.html#prAPReview-2

Re-reviewed at head `5ea51b4899` (previously `3a5588b3f7`). **Every finding from the previous round is resolved** — including the blocker where a refused run wrote no log at all, now fixed by moving the whole selection block below `exec >>"$LOG"`, with a test that drives the real script rather than `--dry-run` and a mutation pinning it. Both numbers in the commit message reproduce: 212 tests pass, and `mutate.py` reports 0 of 88 mutations unaccounted for.

**REQUEST CHANGES**, on the new pre-flight rather than on anything that was open before.

### BUG — [`runner/bin/run-reviewprs.sh:406-409`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/APReview/blob/5ea51b4899aee4f195b68266cb33dcb6f9b5c835/runner/bin/run-reviewprs.sh#L406)

The pre-flight's abort path prints `ABORTING: permission pre-flight failed` and `exit 1` with no `finish=<iso> status=<name>` line, so a refused run shows on the dashboard as still running. `make-runs-page.py:94-95` states the invariant in as many words — "Every early exit prints `finish=<iso> status=<name>`" — and `:100` only sets `finish` from such a line. Both passes reproduced it end to end: a real refusal returns 1 and the generated page renders `running` with `finish=None`. The `gh` check five lines below at `:413-417` *does* emit `status=no-gh-auth`, so the omission is inconsistent within the same file.

Two things I got wrong on first pass and the Codex validation corrected, so the finding is narrower than it first looked: the misclassification is not permanent — the row ages out of the 10-day dashboard window — and the bare `exit 1` is already on `main`. What this PR adds is a new and much more likely trigger for it, and one that fires on exactly the unprepared-box path below. It is still the same class of defect this branch just spent a round fixing: a refusal that reads as a hung run. `echo "finish=$(date -Is) status=preflight-failed"` before the exit, plus teaching `make-runs-page.py` the status; `:196` (`cd` failure) has the same shape and those two are the only non-dry-run exits in the file without a status line.

### BUG — [`runner/bin/run-reviewprs.sh:396-399`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/APReview/blob/5ea51b4899aee4f195b68266cb33dcb6f9b5c835/runner/bin/run-reviewprs.sh#L396)

The credential guard is a bare substring match, and the rule its own error message tells you to add does not protect the directory.

`if auth and not any(auth in r or "review/auth" in r for r in deny)` accepts *any* deny entry containing the substring. The Codex pass got a clean pre-flight from an `Edit` rule, and from `Read(//elsewhere/review/auth/**)`. Worse, the FATAL at `:399` suggests `Read(<absolute path>/**)` with one leading slash, while Claude Code's permission syntax needs `//` for a filesystem-root path — so the suggested rule is interpreted relative to the settings directory, guards the wrong location, and still satisfies the check. The inconsistency is visible inside this PR: the fixture at `test_runner_guard.py:148` uses the two-slash form. That fixture then targets `/review/auth` rather than the test's own temporary credential directory, so the test passes for the wrong reason and the `auth in r` branch is never exercised. And it fails the other way too — the Codex pass found the check **rejects** `Read(~/review/**)`, which is valid and broader. Validate the tool and the covered path rather than matching a substring, and make the suggested rule one that works.

Separately, worth saying in `docs/review-box.md:216-220`, which currently reads as though the rule closes the hole: a deny rule is a guardrail, not containment. The suggested rules stop an obvious `Read` or `cat`; `head`, `grep`, `python3 -c` and `tar` are not covered. The alternative from last round — `auth/` outside `$REVIEW_ROOT`, so it is not inside `--add-dir` at all — remains the only version that actually contains it. The check also covers the Claude agent only; the skill launches `codex exec` with no sandbox flag over the same untrusted PR content.

### ISSUE — the new requirement has no setup step

Because `SETTINGS="$CLAUDE_DIR/settings.json"` (`:379`) is the *selected account's* settings, every Claude account any role can select needs the rule — the fixture writes it to both `claude-ardupilot` and `claude-personal`, so you clearly know. It is described in prose at `docs/review-box.md:216-220`, and the Codex pass is right that this passage is inside the Accounts section, so "documented nowhere" was too strong. What is missing is a **rule to copy** and a migration note: the Install block at `:29-53` and `README.md:129` (which mentions only the `git push` denials) have neither. With otherwise valid accounts carrying only the old denials, the Codex pass reproduced permission aborts for `all`, `followup` and `rsync`. Since merging this repo *is* the deploy, that is every slot — and by the first finding, each one shows as running. Suggest putting the exact rules in the Install block and in `review-auth.sh login`'s output, which is already the "how to set an account up" command. (Codex accounts need no Claude settings, so this applies to the Claude directories only.)

### ISSUE — [`runner/bin/make-runs-page.py:154`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/APReview/blob/5ea51b4899aee4f195b68266cb33dcb6f9b5c835/runner/bin/make-runs-page.py#L154)

`_codex_pick = os.environ.get('CODEX_HOME') or role_dir('codex')` makes the Codex quota card show whichever account the process that last rebuilt the page happened to select. A run exports `CODEX_HOME` for its role and calls `publish-runs-page.sh`; the `*/10` cron entry calls the same script with no `CODEX_HOME` and falls back to the default role. With a fixture holding two accounts at 11 % and 88 %, the same page renders 11 % from cron and 88 % during an rsync run; the Codex pass reproduced the same flip at 10 % / 90 %. The card carries no account name, so nothing distinguishes them. Latent today — both Codex roles point at the same account — but this PR exists to make them differ.

The Codex pass found the same defect one level up, at [`make-runs-page.py:211-215`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/APReview/blob/5ea51b4899aee4f195b68266cb33dcb6f9b5c835/runner/bin/make-runs-page.py#L211): every *historical* run's quota delta is computed from the currently selected account's series, whatever account that run actually spent. A completed account-A run's delta changed from 0 to 20 percentage points when rebuilt under account B's environment. Worth fixing together — either ignore `CODEX_HOME` and always use `role_dir('codex')`, or render one card per account from `account_dirs('codex')` and attribute run rows to the account they used.

Related: `role_dir()` falls back to `~/.codex` when `auth/codex-default` is a dangling link (`os.path.isdir` is false for one), where `review_auth` returns 2 and the runner refuses — so the dashboard would show a healthy meter for a role that will not run.

### ISSUE — [`runner/bin/review-auth.sh:324-343`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/APReview/blob/5ea51b4899aee4f195b68266cb33dcb6f9b5c835/runner/bin/review-auth.sh#L324)

`plain_name` guards `role` and `acct` but never `tool`, and there is no `claude|codex` whitelist in either branch (`TOOLS` at `:40` is used only by `status`). Reproduced in an isolated `$HOME`: `review-auth.sh login ../../work/x personal` returns 0 with no output at all, having run `mkdir -p` and `chmod 700` on `$HOME/work/x-personal` — the `case "$tool"` matches nothing, so it prints nothing and exits successfully. The comment at `:130-133` explains precisely this footgun for the other two arguments. `use` is only *incidentally* safe: a slash in `tool` makes `lockf` name a path whose parent does not exist, so `exec 9>>` fails and it exits 1. One line at the top of both branches:

```sh
case "$tool" in claude|codex) ;; *) echo "unknown tool: $tool" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
```

`plain_name` itself also has no test and no mutation — a validation function with no test is the kind that gets deleted by accident.

### Minor

[`review-auth.sh:267`](https://github.com/ArduPilot/APReview/blob/5ea51b4899aee4f195b68266cb33dcb6f9b5c835/runner/bin/review-auth.sh#L267): `[ A ] || [ B ] && [ C ]` parses as `(A || B) && C`, not `A || (B && C)`. It behaves correctly today only because `acct = role` implies `dir` and `link` are the same path, so `C` is true — the Codex pass confirmed the equivalence with an exhaustive truth table under that invariant. Readability only. Also `review-env.sh:362` is now an orphan fragment mid-sentence (`# shell variables, and a variable`) from this round's edit.

---

The thing I most wanted to check came out clean, so for the record: `review_comment_accounts()` is **byte-identical to `origin/main`**, and `post-comments.py` and `test_post_comments.py` are not touched by this PR at all — so the 2026-09-16 `tridge` → `AP-Review` migration is unaffected and there is no risk of a follow-up run reading no told-head and double-commenting every tracked PR. The switch mechanism itself is also clean: relative target, `--` guarding a leading dash, `-n` rather than bare `-f`, `mv -T` so there is no window where the role link is absent, a refusal when `$link` is a real directory, re-resolution and revert through the same temp+rename idiom, and `auth_root_ok` plus the not-a-symlink check *before* the truncating open of the lock file.


</details>

**Automated review note — AI-generated (Claude), validated against the live diff.** Please sanity-check before acting.

Full report, with what was checked and found clean: https://uav.tridgell.net/DevCallReviews/followups/2026_09_19_1723/devcall_pr_reviews.html#prAPReview-2

### The escaping, which we found from both ends

The cold Codex pass on `e6366444af` found that the deny rule was backslash-escaped once where the CLI unescapes twice — and your audit commit fixes exactly that, independently, in the push that landed while I was reading. So there is nothing to do; I am recording it because it is worth having the arithmetic pinned somewhere other than in our heads.

Verified against the installed CLI rather than argued: `claude` parses a rule's content with `wrr(e) = vrr(e).replaceAll("\\\\","\\")` and `vrr(e) = e.replaceAll("\\(","(").replaceAll("\\)",")")`, then compiles the result as a gitignore pattern with the bundled `ignore` package. A literal backslash therefore needs **four** in the rule text — four → `wrr` → two → gitignore → one — which is what `run-reviewprs.sh:438` and `review-auth.sh:344` now emit and what `denies_auth`'s matching `.replace` at `:403` accepts. `\[` and `\]` stay single-escaped, correctly, because `wrr` leaves them alone. The two-backslash form is now rejected and both directions are pinned.

Also worth saying, because it is the right answer to this whole class of bug: `test_filesystem_normalization_does_not_prove_a_read_pattern` uses `git check-ignore` as an independent oracle for the `.`/`..` rejection, rather than asking the project's own parser whether the project's own parser is right.

### New, all minor

- **NOTE — `runner/bin/claude-usage-probe.sh:21`.** `PROBE_DIR=$(review_auth claude default); PROBE_RC=$?` is the classic `set -e` trap: `review_auth` returns 1 legitimately (no role link, use the tool's own home), and under `-e` the assignment would exit before `PROBE_RC` is read, so an unconfigured default stops probing instead of falling back. **Not live** — nothing in `runner/bin` sets `-e` and `local.conf` is variables only, so today it runs under `set -u` alone and the fallback works. Worth the one line anyway since the file it sources is site-editable:
  ```bash
  PROBE_RC=0
  PROBE_DIR=$(review_auth claude default) || PROBE_RC=$?
  ```
- **NOTE — parentheses are the one escape layer the pre-flight still does not mirror.** `vrr()` unescapes `\(` and `\)`, and Claude's own serializer emits them escaped, but neither generator escapes them and `denies_auth` does not unescape them. For an auth directory named `auth(live)`, the rule Claude itself would write, `Read(//…/auth\(live\)/**)`, matches in the CLI and is *refused* by the pre-flight. The generated bare-paren form works at both ends, so this only bites someone who adds the rule through Claude rather than copying what `login` prints. Pre-existing at both heads and fail-closed, so a nit — but it is the same question as the backslash one and the fix is a `.replace` in the same place.
- **NOTE — `runner/bin/review-env.sh:177`, the `model_providers` skip is keyed on an exact-case `"openai"`.** Reproduced the claims directly against `check_codex_config`: an unused definition is allowed; a selector for it is refused at top level, inside `[profiles.p]`, and in all five config layers; an `openai` redefined with its own `base_url` or `env_key` is refused. The one shape that passes is `model_provider = "openai"` alongside a `[model_providers.OpenAI]` table carrying a foreign `base_url` — the table is skipped on the name test and the selector looks clean. Harmless if codex resolves provider names case-sensitively, which is what a `HashMap` lookup would do, but I could not confirm that end from here. Worth one check rather than a change.
- **NOTE — `mutate.py` is not run by CI.** `tests.yml` runs `bash -n`, `compileall`, the `repos.json` load and the unit tests; there is no reference to `mutate.py`. Pre-existing, but this PR takes the mutation set from 88 to 131 and leans on it as the evidence that each guard is pinned, so the gap is more load-bearing than it was: a later change can unpin a mutation and only a manual run will notice.
